confidence_notes: I ran six searches in total, one of them the RBA lookup. They found only travel-blog price ranges for Leh meals (budget about Rs 150-300, mid-range about Rs 250-700 per person). For drinks, one roughly 2023-era guide gave beer at about Rs 320 (Lehchen 500 ml Rs 400) and cocktails at about Rs 600, which I inflated modestly to July 2026. No cost-of-living index covered Leh, and no Leh cappuccino or wine-by-the-glass prices turned up. Coffee is inferred from a Rs 130 latte review plus general knowledge. Wine is set at about 1.4x beer, below the cocktail price, from general Indian price relationships. Draught beer is scarce in Leh, so a standard bottled or pint domestic beer is assumed. INR prices were converted at an assumed Rs 90-92 per USD from general knowledge, not a searched rate. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect live listings, and seasonal variance is wide.
comparable_city_reasoning: No database comparable city was used. Prices come from Leh-specific INR ranges found in search and general knowledge of Indian Himalayan tourist hubs (for example Manali and McLeod Ganj), with a remote-location and July peak-season premium. Accommodation is the least certain part of that comparison.
